neighbours.label: brand or product names of medicines and medical devices inside medication lists
fire: For mild pain, take acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil, Motrin) as directed.
Antihistamines such as loratadine (Claritin) or cetirizine (Zyrtec) can ease the itching.
Her doctor switched her from omeprazole (Prilosec) to esomeprazole (Nexium) last spring.
Pack a travel kit with bandages, Neosporin ointment and a bottle of Pepto-Bismol.
Patients using warfarin (Coumadin) should avoid large amounts of leafy greens.
Nasal sprays such as fluticasone (Flonase) work best when used every day.
The clinic gave him a prescription for sertraline (Zoloft) and a follow-up visit.
Some people with allergies carry an epinephrine auto-injector such as the EpiPen.
quiet: For mild pain, take a common pain reliever with food and plenty of water.
Antihistamines can ease the itching if they are taken before bedtime each day.
Her doctor switched her to a stronger stomach medicine last spring.
Pack a travel kit with bandages, an antibiotic ointment and an upset stomach remedy.
Patients taking blood thinners should avoid large amounts of leafy greens.
Nasal sprays work best when they are used every day during allergy season.
The clinic gave him a prescription for an antidepressant and a follow-up visit.
Some people with severe allergies carry an emergency shot with them at all times.

notes: Card: peaks inside brand names in parentheses (Ventolin, ProAmatine, Transderm Scop, Robitussin-DM), Medicare Part D, and 'with a portable device'. Near misses keep the medical list style with generic descriptions and no brand names.
